title: Dynamics-Aware Gradient Clipping: Separating Feedback from Threshold Scheduling
content: Adaptive gradient clipping can improve training without establishing that its feedback signals are useful. We examine Dynamics-Aware Gradient Clipping (DAGC), a bounded threshold controller driven by clipping exposure and consecutive-gradient alignment. Its exposure term tightens clipping when clipping is already frequent. We show that an interior target-exposure equilibrium is unstable in a stationary mean-field model, even with exponential smoothing. We then compare the frozen controller with tuned clipping rules, an alignment ablation, and a predetermined threshold schedule on FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10, using validation-only calibration and twelve paired confirmation seeds in each of three conditions.These controls separate threshold scheduling from evidence for an online feedback mechanism; the analysis does not claim convergence of the coupled training dynamics.
